# Write a mapper

You are writing a deterministic mapper from one source system's FOLIO record items into the consumer's app views in `in/views/views.d.ts`.

## What you have (all under `in/`)

- `in/schema/riverside-doc-v1.d.ts`: the source system's schema. This is the only documentation of the source.
  Its docstrings say what every field and code means; read all of it.
- `in/views/`: the target view definitions, written by the consumer. Their docstrings are the
  specification of the output: which rows to emit, which to leave out, units, statuses, time rules.
- `in/samples/`: 8 sample items from 1 patients of this source, in FOLIO Markdown form
  (frontmatter = envelope, then narrative, then the `json payload` block). `in/samples/samples.json` has
  the same items in JSON form, grouped by patient: that is the form your function receives.
- `in/harness/`: `sh in/harness/check.sh [asOf]` type-checks your mapper (strict, no Node/Bun types) and runs
  it on the sample patients, printing the rows.

## The task

Write `out/transform.ts` exporting

```ts
export function transform(items: FolioItem[], asOf: string): ViewRows
```

(the type `Transform` in `in/views/views.d.ts`). It receives every item this source
published for ONE patient, in no particular order, including items that were later superseded or
retracted, and a local date `asOf` (`YYYY-MM-DD`). It returns the rows describing this source's record
as of the end of that day.

Your mapper will be run, unchanged, on many other patients of this source whose records contain
situations the samples do not show. Rely on the schema's documentation for those, not only on the
samples. Nobody will review the output by hand; a mapper that runs cleanly but reads a field wrongly
produces wrong clinical data.

## Rules

- `out/transform.ts` is self-contained TypeScript. Its only allowed import is
  `import type { … } from "../in/views/views"` (and `"../in/views/views"`). No other imports.
- Deterministic: no clock (`Date.now()`, `new Date()` without an argument), no randomness, no network, no
  file system, no environment. Parsing dates with `Date.parse`/`new Date(string)` and `Intl` time-zone
  formatting are fine.
- It must type-check (`sh in/harness/check.sh`) and must not throw on input it does not expect: skip
  what it cannot read.
- You may write and run your own tests or scratch scripts under `out/` with `bun`. Only
  `out/transform.ts` is used.

When you are done, reply with a few lines on the judgment calls you made.
#!/bin/sh
# Type-check out/transform.ts (strict, no Node/Bun types), then run it on the samples.
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.."
bun node_modules/typescript/lib/tsc.js -p in/harness/tsconfig.json
bun in/harness/run.ts "$@"
// Runs out/transform.ts on the sample patients and prints the rows. Usage: bun in/harness/run.ts [asOf]
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { transform } from "../../out/transform.ts";
const groups: { patient: string; items: unknown[] }[] = JSON.parse(readFileSync(new URL("../samples/samples.json", import.meta.url), "utf8"));
const asOf = process.argv[2] ?? "2026-10-13";
for (const g of groups) console.log(JSON.stringify({ patient: g.patient, asOf, rows: (transform as (i: unknown[], a: string) => unknown)(g.items, asOf) }, null, 2));

export { check };

**Reason for admission:** euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis.

**History of present illness.** The patient has type 2 diabetes and takes empagliflozin 10 mg daily at home. They came to the ED with nausea, malaise and fast breathing. <ref id="precipitant">The ketoacidosis was precipitated by prolonged fasting for religious observance while continuing the SGLT2 inhibitor</ref>. On the 14:28 panel sodium was 132, potassium 4.8, chloride 94, bicarbonate 11, anion gap 27, urea nitrogen 26, creatinine 1.85, eGFR 40 and glucose 192. An insulin infusion at 0.1 units/kg/h was started at 15:22 together with dextrose 5% in lactated Ringer's at 150 mL/h, both still running.

**Allergies:** lisinopril (cough).

**Exam.** At 18:52: BP 114/68, HR 94, RR 21, temperature 99.2 F, SpO2 95%. Deep, rapid respirations; mucous membranes dry. Abdomen soft.

**Assessment and plan**

1. <ref id="dx_dka">Euglycemic DKA, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated</ref>. Continue the insulin infusion per protocol with the dextrose-containing fluid, since glucose is near normal. Serial metabolic panels. <ref id="med_empagliflozin">Hold empagliflozin.</ref>
2. <ref id="dx_pancreatitis">Acute pancreatitis ruled out</ref>: lipase 41.
3. Diabetes: <ref id="med_metformin">hold metformin while acidotic and NPO</ref>; resume when able.
4. Volume depletion: <ref id="med_hydrochlorothiazide">hold hydrochlorothiazide for volume depletion</ref>, to resume when able.
5. Hypertension: <ref id="med_losartan">continue losartan</ref>.

content.text: Behavior across dates is sensible. Next, a quick robustness test with malformed input, supersession and retraction:

I wrote `out/transform.ts`. It passes `sh in/harness/check.sh`, and its output on the sample patient is correct at several `asOf` dates. I also ran it on malformed input (nothing thrown), on retracted items, and on a made-up lab panel with a preliminary result, two race-specific eGFRs and glucose in mmol/L. The schema file has no docstrings at all, so I worked out what each field means from the field names, the sample narratives and the view spec.

Judgment calls:

- **Medications:** every Riverside document restates the full home-med list, so I treat the latest current document that has `home_med` entries as the list. Documents are ordered by `effective_end`, falling back to `effective`. That puts the discharge summary last, even though its `effective` is the admission time.
  - **Status mapping:** `not_reconciled` → unknown; `continue`, `new` and `changed` → active; `held` and `stopped` map directly.
  - **Empagliflozin:** it stays **held** even with `restart_advice: advise_against`, because the source records it as held and leaves room for a future re-challenge.
- **Medication dates and reasons:** `status_since` is the date of the earliest document in the unbroken run with the same status. So the 2023 losartan hold dates from the H&P on 4/9, not the discharge, and metformin resumed at discharge is active since 2023-04-12. For a plain `continue` the source never says when the drug started, so I leave the date out. `status_reason_text` is the most recent `instructions` in that run. `stop_reason` comes only from clear keywords in that text.
- **Dose:** `dose_text` is the amount per dose. I only multiply by the tablet count in `sig` when `dose_text` just repeats the tablet strength.
- **Hospital-only orders:** I never report `inpatient_med` entries (IV fluids, insulin drips, inpatient glargine), and I drop any `home_med` that looks like an IV or infusion.
- **Problems:** entries for the same condition are merged by ICD-10 code, then the Riverside dx code, then the label. Status comes from the latest diagnosis entry that is active, resolved or ruled out. Working-only conditions and ones whose latest such entry is ruled out are dropped, so "R/O pancreatitis" is not reported. AKI and hyperkalemia appear as resolved. `history` entries count as active unless worded as past or resolved, and `onset_text` is used only when it parses as a date.
- **Drug-caused diagnoses:** a label like "…, SGLT2 inhibitor-associated" (or a T-code adverse-effect entry) also produces an allergy row. The class is resolved to the single matching drug on that document's med list, so empagliflozin gets RxNorm 1545653 and is recorded as a serious adverse event, non-immune, high criticality, reaction "Euglycemic DKA".
- **Allergies:** reaction type and mechanism are inferred from the reaction text, so lisinopril cough becomes a side effect, non-immune. Severity mild → low, severe → high, and moderate → unknown, which is the least certain of these choices.
- **Labs:** one row per accession, test and collection time, keeping the copy with the highest status (corrected outranks final, which outranks preliminary). Units are converted to the view's units. A result is skipped if it isn't a number, its unit isn't recognised, or its specimen is wrong for the analyte. The eGFR equation is read from the test name before the LOINC code, and a race-specific eGFR is dropped when a race-free one exists for the same specimen.
- **Vitals:** the same reading restated in several documents is reported once. Readings within 15 minutes of each other form one set, with a later BP going in `repeat_*`. Everything is set to `hospital`, since this source only has ED and inpatient encounters.
- **Sensitivity:** the schema has no restriction flag, so I tag only by plain category, using ICD-10 code ranges and drug or condition keywords. Nothing in the sample is tagged.

`out/scratch.ts` is a scratch test file of mine and isn't used by the harness.
